label: 4th original token after an r/n/f-initial, s-heavy prefix (e.g. r s x [1])
explanation: Sparse feature (about 0.015% of steps) that fires almost only in the original phase, mostly at t=3 (70% of mass) and t=4 (23%). It never fires in the copy phase or at t<2. It looks like a conjunction over the prefix tokens: the first token is r/n/f/a/s, the next tokens come from {s,f,x,l,d,3,n,v}, and the current input is 1/k/z/y/p/s/b. The strongest examples are r s x [1], n s s [1], f s 3 [1] and a n s l [1]. Input 1 gives the highest activations (top activation 0.20). The exact 4-token pattern at t=3 has precision of about 0.78 but recall of only about 0.28. Shifted versions of the window (t=4-5, e.g. a s v f [p]) and nearby variants (x f 3 [1], r s 2 [z]) also fire, at lower magnitude (about 0.55 of max). Broader prefix-set predicates reach recall 0.83 but precision below 0.05. It behaves like an additive hidden-state direction that no simple boolean predicate captures well. It does not fire on repeated tokens later in the sequence or on long prefixes (t>=6).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=r (+4.24), prev_tok=s (+4.00), prev2_tok=s (+3.85), prev_tok=l (+3.75), orig0=a (+3.64), prev_tok=x (+3.19). Lower it: correct=1 (-7.06), orig_idx=-1 (-2.71).
